top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is a distinct physical idea (cancelling light shifts so thousands of neutral atoms can be held in the Lamb-Dicke regime free of Doppler and recoil shifts), separate from the 2005 frequency comb and the 2012 single-ion control. It has been reproduced across several laboratories and has reached uncertainties near 10^-18. Katori holds the concept and first demonstration and Ye the systematic and many-body coherence work, so the two-name allocation with a citation naming the lattice principle is defensible. The remaining concerns (overlap with earlier precision-measurement prizes, omitted contributors such as Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and Hinkley) are real but do not outweigh awarding a mature, reproduced result over no award.
recusal_note: No conflict for B018 apparent from my profile. As WACQT director and a superconducting-circuits theorist at Chalmers I would recuse on B008 (circuit QED), which is not in this slate.
